653.t: Old brass band dress code and his return to fireman's caps
653.s: Traditional dress was white cap, black tie and pants; he went back to older military-style uniforms.
653.ch: Brass band style, leadership and recording
653.q: The dress code, the dress code when I came up, man. You wore a white cap for gay things and happy things. You wore a black top cap for cornerstone laying, maybe playing in a church and a funeral. You wore a white shirt and a black tie. Clean, black pants and shoes. Black shoes. Okay.

653.t: The Olympia t-shirt, Roman collar uniforms and insisting on dress
653.s: The first brass band t-shirt from a Toronto trip and the uniforms still used, plus his insistence on dressing well.
653.ch: Brass band style, leadership and recording
653.q: You know what I'm saying? I went back to the old fireman's cap, which was used in the early days for the circus band and the other bands that performed. And to me, musicians should be dressed. All the time be dressed. And I stress this with my band up to today. Don't come on my bandstand and don't…

181.t: Hobgoblin silk gowns and night parades
181.s: Hobgoblins wore blue silk gowns and caps, paraded at night and never played funerals.
181.q: What kind of uniforms did the Hobgoblin band wear? Uniforms? Uh-huh. You said they were different. Oh, they had the—they had the—the silk gown, you know.

390.t: First uniformed big band in New Orleans
390.s: Desvigne believes his was the first big band in New Orleans to wear uniforms, which others then copied.
390.q: I think I was, if I'm not mistaken. But you didn't think of Dixie. But I do know that we were the first one, the big band, to actually have really uniformed the band, all uniformed, you know. Yeah, that uniform. We had tuxed and then we had some blazes and, very good, looked very good. And after…

248.t: Band uniforms in New Orleans: Ory's blues, Eagle brown, Imperial
248.s: Discussion of band uniforms: Eagle Band brown, Imperial and Ory's blue, caps, and Lil's uniform in Chicago.
248.q: Well, I was trying to introduce them. And there's Eagle Band. Eagle Band had brown uniforms. We had a revelation blue uniform.

430.t: Brass band and Eagle Band uniforms, caps and trousers
430.s: Description of band uniforms in the old days, the Eagle Band's green outfits, and complaints about mismatched uniforms today.
430.q: Oh, in those days, well, they had uniforms. All the bands had uniforms. They had blue uniforms. One band I seen had, you know, no, I wouldn't say one band, no. Because the Eagle Band, I mean, I mean the band, not the brass band, the Eagle Band. The orchestra. The orchestra. They had a green outfit…

601.t: The Golden Rule band and the Pacific band's uniforms
601.s: Tom recalls the short-lived Golden Rule band downtown. Martin counters that the Pacific band had uniforms before it, with scoop hats and plumes, probably blue.
601.q: Pico. That's right. That's what Slowdrag wanted to tell me. That was the first band. Had an uniform. But I know better. The first band had an uniform before the Golden Rule. You take the Pacific had an uniform. Oh, the Pacific. Yeah, that's the Grass Band. That's right. Yeah, the Grass Band. You…

138.t: Looking at an 1896 photo; Laine's fancy uniform
138.s: They find a faded 1896 photo of the band, and Laine says he refused the heavily decorated uniform the major offered.
138.q: That's the, that's the, that's the picture. And there he is. You see, it's kind of faded. We had it taken. Is that his picture? That's him. Mm-hmm. Yeah.

151.s: Reason says they wore uniforms at first and then regular suits.
151.ch: Union, New Orleans and King Oliver
151.q: When I first went with him, we wore uniforms. And after that, we just wore your regular suits. And we'd wear white shirts. And stuff like stuff like

629.s: A photo shows Picou in a brass band cap, which he says came from the Onward band.
629.q: All of us had to have a cap like that.

857.t: Uniforms: tuxedo suits worn only for advertising
857.s: The Tuxedo band wore regular brass band dress in parades and tuxedo suits only to advertise dances.
857.q: Well we wore them on the street when we'd be advertising, you know, playing for a dance like that.

800.s: He describes braided coats and blue uniforms of the Golden Rule band and that Perez and Excelsior had two uniforms.
800.q: Same kind of uniform. Well, same kind of... Well, on the contrary, they started using newer uniform than they did a long time ago.

182.t: Band uniforms for parades and funerals
182.s: He describes uniforms and caps for parades and funerals in Henry Allen's band.
182.ch: Brass bands: Eureka and Henry Allen
182.q: Joe, Joe, Joe Lizard. Joe Lizard. He was the leader of the Excelsior band. Yeah, I know the band, but they used to wear green suits. What kind of suits did Henry Allen's band wear? Well we used to wear, we used to have them kind of a, we used to wear white pants and blue pants, you know, all white…

635.t: The Magnolia Band's uniforms and caps
635.s: Description of green and blue military-style uniforms with gold-lettered caps marking leader and manager, and how the cap helped him with girls.
635.q: And Magnolia band manager. Uh-huh. Now when anybody come up and want to see the manager, let's look at the capcorder. Now that's where I used to make a lot of girls. The girl wouldn't speak to me, she wouldn't say with my instrument. I'd go and put the cap on and say, oh why are you playing? And I…

830.t: Old band uniforms and Papa's banner
830.s: They describe the old blue braided uniforms with mandarin collars and ask about the whereabouts of the banner.
830.q: Well, that picture of the banner, yes. They don't have those anymore for the banners. They didn't give it to you. Who didn't you give it to? Junior gave it to you. You gave it to Junior.

301.t: Uncle's brass band caps from the Excelsior band
301.s: Dutre recalls a keepsake of band caps from the Excelsior brass band, lost when his grandmother found them.
301.q: No, I never did see Honoré or Peter. But, I do know that he played in a lot of the top brass bands like that. Yeah. I think it was Excelsior one band he played with before he left there. Yeah, I didn't even know. Because I had all the caps, he left me all the caps at the house. Well, he had the old…

15.s: Musicians wore tuxedos because contracts required it; Howard did not need to change when he joined Oliver.
15.q: Well I went down there and I said what are you wearing? Tuxedo. I didn't have to do no change. I just went around and put the same tuxedo on and went to work.

306.t: Uniforms of the Tuxedo, Eureka and other bands; borrowed and secondhand outfits
306.s: Rene describes the Tuxedo's blue uniform, the Eureka's black pants and white shirts, fireman caps, and buying cheap tuxedos for the Jefferson Tea Room.
306.ch: Uniforms, funeral music and horn styles
306.q: a lot of old things way back, boy. That's a parade outfit here. They never changed a customer costume, bro. They still got the same identity. Still got them white top caps, double-soar handkerchief around them and everything. They ain't done no better than uniform, I tell you. They're the same…

357.t: Straw hats, uniforms and the band's volunteer spirit
357.s: Tuba and trombone slide hit the hats, so hats are worn only for photographs; he stresses the band plays free and wants it easy for them.
357.q: I’ve always insisted that the straw hats be worn. And it’s been, I think a boon to us because our publicity is very good. The pictures of us in the Alumni Review for example with the hats on are terrific, it’s a uniform thing. But lately I’m getting a lot of resistance to wearing the hats. And two…

108.t: Band uniforms and pride in appearance
108.s: Uniforms of Cab, Duke, Kirby and Hite, and why audiences came to see how the bands dressed.
108.q: Oh, we had uniforms, yeah. Each band tried to outdo the other. Every band had its own distinctive style. Cab’s band, they wore tails. They were very classy. Duke, same thing. Real class. John Kirby’s band, they wore white tails, black tails, and so forth. Some of the other bands had suits. They’d…
